clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's death in June 1991, within three years: your wrist injury and drop from the conservatory in the first term, your drift through late 1991 and 1992, your mother's marriage to Desmond in October 1992, your sister Tara's birth in July 1990, and your move through a bleak spell at community college before the exchange to Portugal in early 1994. You said you leaned hard on Rafe once you arrived at the conservatory in September 1991; within weeks the injury stopped your playing and Rafe moved out. You were lost and low through the following months, high most days, absorbed in fixing radios. By the time you began swimming and tearing through your coursework in Portugal, the family had settled into a new shape with Desmond and Tara, and your footing came back.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's diagnosis with bowel cancer, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis in 2001 or 2002, over more than two years: you ran out of steam for performing that autumn, sank into a deep depression once you and Marisol split in late 2003, and could not face your family. You moved to Gull Harbour in September 2002 and were on poor terms with family and friends; within months you met Marisol at a winter party and left for Fenwick to live with her in June 2003. The split came within the year, and you returned to Thornbury that winter, minding a house near Hamish, hardly moving from the sofa. You relied on friends rather than family through those months; Corbin and Russell talked several times during your stay. Your grandmother spent her final months in your mother's home, and you dropped in briefly on the way to the airport in January 2004, hung over and in haste. She died of the cancer in February 2004. That spring you began swimming to help you sleep and returned to your therapist; the gradual recovery pointed you toward nursing.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008–2009
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within a year: you withdrew from your mother, too drained for conversation at Alder Creek in July 2008 where you were building with Silas. She drove out regardless of your repeated word that the timing was wrong; the visit went wrong and she never got inside. You stopped speaking to her when you moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school that August, a silence that held for roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke in January 2009 with months of rehabilitation. The cutoff eased once you had settled into your studies and the household rhythm steadied.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, over two and a half years: your contact with your mother eased off slightly once Wren came along; your anxiety climbed steadily through 2019 as you felt you ought to be driving your projects forward, and you started a sleeping pill in October. In that same month, Wren was swamped by a street party, a fundraising dinner, and the drive to the lake for her mother's retirement party; she called her father and brother all day, and the family moved as one. Once a plan was laid the dinner went well, but at the lake weekend you awoke from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose. Your sleep is worst around her family; you feel you don't belong. Your sister Tara had a baby on the way, your cousin Bella was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, and your aunt Imogen's memory slipped further; she lashes out when muddled.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
